what: Do the publisher's vLLM command for Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 and that command with its documented speculation option start and serve on one H100 with vLLM 0.34.0. One server per check (tools/poc-modal/modal_gpu.py --action check). No speed is measured.
findings: The command as published does not start: vLLM 0.34.0 refuses its default of 1,024 requests at once against 904 recurrent-state (Mamba) cache blocks on one H100. vLLM 0.22.1 had 818.
With --max-num-seqs 512 added it starts in 264 s, refuses a request without its key, answers, calls a tool, and exports every engine metric family the control plane reads.

The publisher's Rust frontend (VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1) serves on this image; on 0.22.1 it exited at startup. It logs that --enable-auto-tool-choice has no effect in the Rust frontend and that it cannot run the model's response template (a regex with look-ahead), and uses the named reasoning and tool parsers; the tool call in the check succeeded.

With the publisher's documented speculation option (--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}) added, it starts in 339 s as architecture Qwen3_5MTP, passes the same checks, and exports the speculation counters: over the check's three answers 246 of 408 drafted tokens were accepted. Three requests show that the drafter works and is counted; they are not an acceptance rate for any traffic. vLLM warns that more than one speculative token runs the same prediction layer several times and may lower acceptance.
